skills.description: Two-axis review of a branch, PR, or work-in-progress diff against a fixed point: standards compliance and spec fidelity. Use when asked to review changes, review since a commit or branch, or check whether a diff implements the originating issue without scope creep. Do not use for reviewing generated code you cannot inspect or for a single line whose behavior is already covered by an existing review.

Design deep modules with clean seams and testable interfaces. Use when designing or improving a module interface, deciding where a seam belongs, making code more testable or AI-navigable, or reviewing an architecture that is becoming shallow. Do not use for visual design, product copy, or one-line implementation changes with no interface decision.

React composition patterns for flexible component APIs. Use when refactoring components with boolean prop proliferation, building reusable component libraries, designing compound components or context providers, or reviewing component architecture. Do not use for page-level data fetching, CSS-only changes, or React Native components.

A disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user asks to diagnose or debug something, or reports behavior that is broken, throwing, failing intermittently, or slow. Do not use for applying a fix whose cause is already proven, or for style-only changes.

Security-focused review of PRs, commits, and diffs. Use when reviewing a code change for vulnerabilities, regressions, removed validation, auth or crypto changes, blast radius, or missing test coverage; also use when checking whether a change reintroduces a previously fixed bug. Do not use for greenfield code with no baseline, documentation-only changes, or formatting-only diffs.

Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, recording or revising an ADR, or resolving overloaded terms across code and documentation. Do not use for merely reading a glossary, implementation-only refactors, or project management status updates.

Choose and run the correct .NET test command for a repository. Use when running or explaining dotnet tests, including filtered runs, single projects, xUnit v2/v3, MSTest, NUnit, TUnit, VSTest vs Microsoft Testing Platform, coverage, TRX, diagnostics, crash dumps, or hang dumps. Do not use for identifying the platform alone, writing test code, or migrating a test framework.

Create and modify ASP.NET Core Web API endpoints with correct HTTP semantics, DTOs, OpenAPI metadata, and error handling. Use when working with Minimal APIs or controllers in .NET, request and response types, OpenAPI wiring, centralized error handling, or .http test files. Do not use for general C# style, EF Core query optimization, Blazor, gRPC, or SignalR.

Configure Python projects with modern tooling and secure defaults. Use when creating a Python project or package, writing standalone scripts with dependencies, setting up pyproject.toml, configuring uv, ruff, ty, pytest, or pre-commit tooling, or migrating from pip, Poetry, mypy, black, and isort. Do not use for exploratory notebooks, non-Python projects, or repositories whose maintainers require legacy tooling.

Verify Next.js runtime behavior after editing app code. Use when a change must be confirmed in a running Next.js app, not just compiled or typechecked, and when the project has a running next dev server with the Next.js MCP endpoint and agent-browser available. Do not use for projects below Next.js 16.3, webpack-only dev setups, or changes that can be fully verified by a unit test.

Postgres schema, query, locking, connection, and security practices for PostgreSQL running anywhere. Use when creating or changing tables, indexes, constraints, migrations, RLS policies, SQL functions, or queries, or when diagnosing slow queries, timeouts, lock contention, bloat, or connection exhaustion. Do not use for other database engines without checking their differences.

Write, review, and debug property-based tests. Use when tests should cover a whole input domain instead of a hand-picked list: encode/decode pairs, parsers, canonicalizers, validators, numeric types, comparators, data structures, or invariants. Also use when judging whether existing property tests assert anything real or when a generator shrunk a counterexample. Do not use for coverage-guided binary fuzzing, mutation-testing campaigns, static analysis, benchmarking, or end-to-end UI tests.

Performance and correctness rules for React and Next.js from Vercel Engineering. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle boundaries, or rendering behavior, and when investigating waterfalls, bundle size, or re-render costs. Do not use for React Native, non-React UI frameworks, or performance work without a React component in scope.

Evaluate code review feedback before implementing it. Use when the user pastes PR comments, audit findings, or external reviewer suggestions and asks to apply them, especially when feedback is unclear, conflicting, or technically questionable. Do not use for writing a fresh review from scratch or for applying a change the user has already fully specified.

Test-driven development for features and bug fixes. Use when the user asks for TDD, red-green-refactor, test-first implementation, integration tests, or behavior-focused tests, and when a change needs a regression test before the implementation. Do not use for exploratory spikes, throwaway prototypes, or changes with no observable behavior to pin down.

Isolate feature work in a Git worktree before implementation or plan execution. Use when starting work that needs isolation from the current workspace, when parallel branches would collide, or when the harness offers a native worktree tool. Do not use when the user explicitly wants to work in place, or when the repository is not a Git checkout.

Require fresh evidence before claiming work is complete, fixed, or passing. Use when about to commit, open a PR, hand work to another agent, or say a test, build, linter, or requirement is satisfied. Do not use for interim progress updates that make no completion claim.

Review UI code against Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines. Use when asked to review UI, check accessibility, audit design or UX, or verify forms, navigation, animation, typography, images, and interactive states against current web interface rules. Do not use for backend-only changes, mobile native UI, or visual design work with no interface code to inspect.

Write documents that coding agents consume predictably. Use when creating or editing a skill, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or a document reached by a context pointer, and when an agent ignores, over-reads, or misapplies an instruction file. Do not use for human marketing copy, API reference generated from code, or release notes with no agent-facing component.

Write implementation plans that another engineer or agent can execute without guessing. Use when a spec or set of requirements exists for a multi-step task and code has not been touched yet, especially when the work spans several files, interfaces, or commits. Do not use for one-line changes, open-ended brainstorming, or exploration with no implementation target.
